table.name: battle
table.purpose: Battles between the Bulgarian Empire and the Latin Empire (Fourth Crusade era, early 13th century). Each row is one battle/siege, with commanders on both sides, date, and outcome. Referenced by ship.lost_in_battle and death.caused_by_ship_id (the latter likely a mis-mapped join).

bulgarian_commander.name: bulgarian_commander
bulgarian_commander.description: Name of the commander of the Bulgarian forces in the battle (e.g. Tsars Kaloyan, Boril, Ivan Asen II); 'Unknown' when not recorded.

date.name: battle_date
date.description: Date of the battle, stored as free text with inconsistent precision (full day, month+year, or year only). Note '31 June 1208' is an impossible date (June has 30 days), likely a data error for the Battle of Boruy (July 1208).

id.name: battle_id
id.description: Primary key, surrogate integer id for the battle. Referenced by ship.lost_in_battle (ships lost in that battle). The join to death.caused_by_ship_id is accepted statistically but semantically dubious (a ship id pointing to battle ids).

latin_commander.name: latin_commander
latin_commander.description: Name of the commander of the Latin (Crusader/Latin Empire) forces, e.g. Emperor Baldwin I, Henry I, Boniface of Montferrat, John of Brienne, Thierry de Termond; 'Unknown' when not recorded.

name.name: battle_name
name.description: Name of the battle or siege, e.g. Battle of Adrianople, Siege of Constantinople. Unique per row.

result.name: battle_outcome
result.description: Outcome of the battle: 'Bulgarian victory', 'Latin victory', or 'Two Year Truce' (a negotiated truce ending the engagement).

table.name: death
table.purpose: Casualty records per incident: number killed and injured, the ship (or battle, via ambiguous FK) associated with the event, and a location note. One row per death/casualty incident. The 'note' values are Indian district locations, which conflicts with the naval ship/battle context, so the table's real-world domain is mixed or the data is synthetic; the structural meaning is still clear.

caused_by_ship_id.name: caused_by_ship_id
caused_by_ship_id.description: Foreign key to ship.id identifying the ship associated with the incident. The join is statistically ambiguous: it also matches battle.id (many_to_one), so it may in some rows reference a battle instead of a ship; the column name favors ship.id.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the death table; unique row identifier.

injured.name: injured
injured.description: Count of people injured in the incident; mostly 0, max 9.

killed.name: killed
killed.description: Count of people killed in the incident; ranges 0-29.

note.name: note
note.description: Location note for the incident, formatted as 'Place, State' (e.g., 'Dantewada, Chhattisgarh'). These are Indian districts, which is inconsistent with the ship/battle naval context; treated as a free-text location/description field.

table.name: ship
table.purpose: Ships (mostly brigs) lost or captured in battles, with their type, tonnage, location, and final disposition. Each row is one ship lost in a specific battle (linked to battle table).

disposition_of_ship.name: disposition_of_ship
disposition_of_ship.description: How the ship was lost: Captured, Sank, Scuttled, or Wrecked.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the ship table; referenced by death.caused_by_ship_id.

location.name: location
location.description: Geographic location where the ship was lost (e.g., English Channel, Mid-Atlantic, SW Approaches).

lost_in_battle.name: lost_in_battle
lost_in_battle.description: Foreign key to battle.id, identifying the battle in which the ship was lost.

name.name: name
name.description: Name of the ship (e.g., HMS Avon, Lettice, Mary).

ship_type.name: ship_type
ship_type.description: Type/rig of the vessel, including gun count where known (Brig, 18-gun Brig, 8 gun Brig).

tonnage.name: tonnage
tonnage.description: Ship's tonnage as a number (e.g., 225, 391); the value 't' appears where the tonnage is unknown/unrecorded, making the column text rather than numeric.
